explanation: The theorem is about the library's own definitions (ρ₀', inclAdj, chartAlgFin, jChartFin, ρ₀'_jInv). It shows that a specific ring map sends elements of Algebra.adjoin ℤ {j⁻¹} into Algebra.adjoin (ZMod p) {X⁻¹}. The proof is a direct Algebra.adjoin_induction that uses the library's lemma ρ₀'_jInv. Mathlib has no declaration with this content. The closest general principle is the map-of-adjoin result (Algebra.adjoin_image or AlgHom.map_adjoin). It doesn't apply directly, because ρ₀' is not given as an algebra hom on the adjoin and its action on j⁻¹ comes from the library-specific ρ₀'_jInv. I did not run a search of Mathlib.
